headline: Comparative genomics links shark epigenomes, Wnt gene repertoires and intron evolution
label: Comparative Genome Architecture Inference
summary: Chromosome-scale shark genomes, genome-wide intron surveys and 1,961-vertebrate Wnt analyses now enable structural evolution inference at scale.
synthesis: The dominant thread is comparative inference of genome architecture and evolutionary history from large sequence collections. A chromosome-scale, haplotype-phased tiger shark genome is paired with methylomic and hydroxymethylomic profiling, reporting male heterogamety, transposable element expansions and demographic history. A telotron survey across 10,310 eukaryotic genome assemblies identifies spliceosomal introns composed mostly of telomeric repeats and links them to intron gain. A comparative analysis of 38,886 Wnt sequences from 1,961 vertebrates quantifies copy-number variation, whole-genome duplication effects and dN/dS rates. The shared frame is applying comparative and population-level approaches to structural and gene-family change over evolutionary time. What is new is the joint treatment of epigenomic profiling, genome-wide intron surveys and gene repertoire dynamics.
